title: At fixed region content, SWPC M-flare probabilities rose gradually in 2022-2026 by about the removed GOES 0.7 factor; legacy-scale region climatologies under-forecast Cycle 25 by 1.42
abstract: Question: after NOAA removed the GOES 0.7 flux factor in December 2019, did SWPC change its M-class probabilities at the same region content, and how large is the error of region class-rate climatologies across the change? Method: we attributed 54,503 SWPC events with true-scale peaks to 46,754 SWPC Solar Region Summary region-days (1998-2026). We built a Poisson region climatology (McIntosh components, Mount Wilson class, area) trained on Cycles 23-24 and verified it on Cycle 25. We compared SWPC day-1 M probabilities with the climatology probability of the same regions, with persistence controls and 27-day block bootstraps. Results: at fixed region content, the logit of the SWPC probability stayed at the Cycle 24 level in 2020-2021 and then increased each year: +0.18 (2022), +0.37 (2023), +0.52 (2024), +0.72 (2025), +0.76 (2026). Within Cycle 25 the change after March 2025 is a Poisson rate factor of 1.54 (1.41-1.69), close to 1/0.7. A local test around March 2025 gives 1.07 (0.84-1.40), and steps of this size occur in 6% of Cycle 23-24 windows, so we found no single dated step. X-class probabilities changed by 1.10 (0.95-1.30). Region productivity did not increase in 2025-2026 (1.38 against 1.67 in 2020-2024, relative to Cycle 24). A McIntosh climatology trained on legacy-scale counts under-forecasts Cycle 25 M1+ days by 1.42 (1.34-1.51) and X1+ days by 1.52 (1.14-1.92); trained on true-scale counts it gives 1.05 (0.98-1.12) and 1.01. On one scale the calibration still changes by 1.30 (1.17-1.47) from Cycle 24 to 25. Our code reproduces the sibling result of 1.61 times more M flares per region of the same class (1.61, 1.28-1.97); F10.7 reduces it to 1.23 (0.99-1.64). Limitations: SWPC procedures are not public, the region index is a model, the step tests have low power, and Cycle 25 is incomplete.
